memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Cain made love to his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Cain was then building a city, and he named it after his son Enoch. - Gen 4:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Life goes on for Cain. He has a family, and he builds a city - the first city in the Bible - naming it after his son. On the surface this looks like progress and success. And in a sense it is; God's common grace still allows the wanderer to build, create, and multiply.

But notice what is missing. There is no mention of God, no altar, no calling on the Lord's name. Cain, who went out from God's presence, now tries to build permanence and security apart from Him. He wanted a city to replace the home he had lost. It is the story of every human attempt to find lasting security without God at the centre.

We do the same when we pour ourselves into building careers, homes, and reputations while leaving God out. The building itself is not wrong - but a life constructed apart from God is a city with no true foundation (Ps 127:1).

The believer looks for something more lasting. Like Abraham, we are "looking forward to the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God" (Heb 11:10). Build your life, yes - but build it with God at the centre, on the only foundation that lasts, Jesus Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you building your life with God at the centre or on the edges?
- What are you trusting for your security?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, unless You build my life, I labour in vain. Be the foundation and centre of everything I build.
